summary: Google Cloud authors migrate one small Spring sample app (spring-petclinic-genai) from Java to Python with Gemini 2.5 Pro, comparing a vector-RAG baseline (800-char chunks, top-5) against a tree-sitter AST graph in Spanner Property Graph, a context-cached 'architecture skeleton', and parent-first topological ordering. On seven author-defined AST metrics, the graph pipeline lowers a custom hallucination rate and improves dependency/inheritance scores but worsens cyclomatic consistency and docstring preservation; CodeBLEU is ~91% for both.

claims.claim: Graph RAG cuts API hallucination rate from 56.4% to 16.2%.
claims.evidence: Table 1 (Avg Hallucination Rate 56.4% vs 16.2%). The hallucination metric uses a 'Global Lookup' symbol table (§5.3) introduced specifically because the file-level check penalised Graph RAG; one repository, one run at T=0, file count not stated, no variance.

Table 1 matches abstract. DRQ is an import-resolvability check against stdlib + a whitelist; PCC compares regex-extracted Java extends/implements to Python bases (§5.2). Author-defined metrics, not executed tests.
Table 1: 90.6% vs 91.1% while custom metrics diverge. Plausible and consistent with known CodeBLEU criticism, but shown on a single repo.

claims.claim: Standard RAG leads to high compilation failure rates; Graph RAG yields compilable, functional code.
claims.evidence: No compilation, test execution or runtime check is reported; linter StaQ is 100% for both (Table 1). 'Functional' and 'compilable' are unsupported.

claims.claim: Graph context causes 'defensive over-engineering' (CCC 71.6% -> 46.7%) and 'attention dilution' (DP 67% -> 61%).
claims.evidence: Table 1 numbers present; causal explanations are speculation with no analysis of generated code beyond one file (OwnerController CCC 18% vs 84%).

patterns.note: AST-derived code graph context improved dependency/inheritance metrics over naive vector chunks on one Java repo; weak evidence (one repo, custom metrics).
Naive 800-char chunk vector retrieval lost parent classes and cross-file APIs for controllers; but baseline is untuned and given far less context than the graph arm.
tree-sitter AST extraction is the deterministic backbone of the graph.
Topological parent-first migration ordering is a deterministic orchestration step around LLM translation, not a codemod.

methodology.sample: One repository (spring-petclinic-genai, a sample app); number of files not stated; Tables 2-3 show 6 individual files.
methodology.baselines: Standard RAG with recursive 800-char chunks, 150 overlap, text-embedding-004, top-k=5; graph arm also gets a full architecture skeleton, translated parent code and vector fallback, so context volume is confounded.
methodology.variance: Single run per arm; none reported.
methodology.ablations: None (skeleton cache, topological ordering, graph traversal and vector fallback are not separated).
methodology.contamination_controls: None; spring-petclinic is a widely mirrored public repo likely in training data.

standards.artifacts: Only the input repo URL; no pipeline code, prompts, or metric scripts released.

biases.detail: Seven custom metrics and a weighted Migration Quality composite (40/30/20/10) defined by the authors; the hallucination metric was modified after observing it penalised the proposed method.
Untuned naive chunking with k=5 vs a graph arm with whole-repo skeleton plus parent code; no AST-chunked or hybrid baseline.
Claims about compilation/functional viability measured by static import/inheritance checks with no test execution.
spring-petclinic is a famous public repo.
Context caching is motivated by cost/latency but no token, cost or latency numbers are reported.

coi.affiliations: All authors list google.com emails / Google Cloud (Jaiswal, Shukla, Malhotra, Agrawal, Garg, Bhaumik, Puri).
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Google Cloud Spanner Property Graph, Vertex AI Context Caching, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Vertex AI embeddings.
coi.detail: Vendor employees showcasing a pipeline built entirely on their own cloud products; the comparison is method-vs-method on the same stack rather than against a competitor, and the text claims platform-agnosticism, but no independent replication or non-Google implementation.

verdict_reason: Directionally plausible (graph/AST context helps cross-file Java dependencies; CodeBLEU is a poor migration metric) but n=1 repo, single run, untuned confounded baseline, author-invented metrics with no tests, no artifacts, and Google-stack showcasing by Google employees.
applicability: Moderately relevant: it is one of few corpus papers on Java code. For the team, the takeaway is that structural context (AST/graph of inheritance, imports, calls - obtainable via a code graph tool like Gortex or LSP, no Spanner needed) matters more than embedding chunks for cross-file Java work, and that parent-first ordering of dependent changes is a cheap deterministic orchestration trick. It does not show anything about multi-repo graphs (single repo), runtime correctness (no tests ran), or mixed hosts (single Gemini pipeline). Under spec-driven development, treat its metrics as a warning: define acceptance via executed tests/contracts, not CodeBLEU or bespoke static scores.
